fatal_errors: The proposed Y/Hf compositional intervention is unrelated to the target modulation-period and interface-coherency intervention.
The hypothesis substitutes high-temperature oxidation behavior for room-temperature nanoindentation creep.

The cited evidence establishes slower oxide growth and room-temperature tensile properties, but provides no creep measurements or evidence that suppressed Al diffusion through an oxide/depletion zone controls plastic creep.
The proposed mechanism omits the target distinction among coherent interfaces, semicoherent interfaces with misfit dislocations, and grain-boundary-dominated structures.
No stress exponent, creep displacement, steady-state strain rate, or microstructural measurement is proposed to discriminate diffusion/interface-slip creep from dislocation-mediated creep.
explanation: The response is only broadly aligned in discussing an FCC/BCC coating and claiming improved resistance under sustained loading. It reconstructs neither the Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer system nor the modulation-period comparison, room-temperature indentation conditions, semicoherent-interface mechanism, or nonmonotonic optimum at 16 nm. Its comparison and falsification rule could test gross performance, but cannot identify the governing creep mechanism. The cited study supports oxidation resistance through alumina-scale formation and diffusion suppression, plus room-temperature tensile improvement; extrapolating those findings to creep resistance under continuous loading is unsupported.
